answer: In a marketplace where agents trade yarrow grown at an oasis, each seller identity must lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before listing goods. Buyers can prove a double sale by submitting two conflicting receipts signed by that seller, causing its bond to be forfeited. A tide of 10,000 fake sellers therefore requires $1 million in locked capital, and identities caught double selling lose their deposits; creating more names cannot bypass the bond.
